findings.title: Login cache invalidation misses realm-level IdP BROKER_PUBLIC changes
findings.body: registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate returns without invalidating when both old and new models pass getLoginPredicate() and have the same organizationId. For a realm-level IdP (organizationId == null), getLoginPredicate() is true regardless of OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC. However getForLogin(ORG_ONLY, null) populates its cache from a delegate query that searches BROKER_PUBLIC=true without requiring an organization link, so a realm-level IdP with BROKER_PUBLIC=true can be part of that cached result. Changing BROKER_PUBLIC on such an already login-eligible realm-level IdP therefore does not invalidate the ORG_ONLY cache, leaving a stale broker list on the login page until some other login-relevant mutation invalidates it.

findings.title: remove() can leave a stale getById cache entry on alias cache miss
findings.body: When isInvalid(cacheKey) is false and the alias cache entry is null, the removal path does not call registerIDPInvalidation(storedIdp). If the IdP was previously loaded by internal id (cached under that id) but its alias key was never cached or was evicted, idpDelegate.remove(alias) deletes the entity while the internal-id cache entry remains. A subsequent getById(internalId) then returns the deleted IdP. Since storedIdp is now loaded unconditionally at line 100, it should be invalidated in all removal paths.

findings.title: Cleanup registers the wrong alias for created identity providers
findings.body: Line 381 (and similarly line 425) uses testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove instead of the actual idpRep.getAlias(). As a result, the created idp-alias-* identity providers are not removed during cleanup, and remain in the realm for later tests or reruns. This can cause cross-test pollution or duplicate-alias failures, and may also remove an unrelated IdP that actually has the alias 'alias'.
